statement.text: At sea, weather is never a backdrop. Wind rearranges sails, clouds erase distance, and waves turn travel into risk. These works follow the shoreline and open water through changing conditions: the tense interval before a storm, the violence of wreck and surge, and the quieter persistence of vessels and coasts after the weather has passed. Across oil, wash, watercolor, gouache, and print, atmosphere becomes an active force that measures human scale against the sea.

works.title: Ships in a Stormy Sea
works.label: Gray wash and dense linework give wind and cloud as much force as the two ships, which pitch through choppy water. The distant vessel underscores how quickly the storm has swallowed the open sea.

works.title: Storm-Tossed Ships Wrecked on a Rocky Coast
works.label: Violent waves drive several ships toward a jagged coast beneath dark clouds and a sharp flash of light. The wreck turns weather into an immediate collision between vessel, sea, and shore.

works.title: A Rocky Seacoast in a Storm
works.label: Watercolor, gouache, and gum arabic bring a storm-bound rocky coast into the exhibition’s shifting weather sequence. Its title fixes the shoreline as a place exposed to the force of the sea.

works.title: The Much Resounding Sea
works.label: In black etched, drypoint, and roulette marks, the sea is named for its sound rather than its calm. The print makes the water’s persistent roar a physical presence at the edge of travel and land.

works.title: Ships and Sailing Boats Leaving Le Havre
works.label: Ships and smaller sailing boats depart Le Havre, placing working movement on water at the center of the scene. Against the exhibition’s storms and wrecks, their departure marks the more ordinary but still weather-dependent business of leaving shore.

works.title: Spring Tide, Rocks of Zion (Grande maree, rochers de Sion, Vendee)
works.label: The title identifies a spring tide at the rocks of Zion, where rising water remakes the boundary between coast and sea. Etching gives that tidal pressure a spare, graphic form.

works.title: Weymouth Bay
works.label: Weymouth Bay offers a coastal interval in the exhibition, set apart from the titles of storm and wreck. Its mezzotint surface makes atmosphere and distance central to the bay’s changing condition.

works.title: Jonah Thrown into the Stormy Sea
works.label: A biblical figure is cast into stormy water, making the sea the site of sudden danger rather than passage. Engraving carries the crisis through a scene in which weather determines human vulnerability.
